id.description: The event's own id. Stable across a retry of the same event.

ts.description: When it happened, by Chips' clock. Stamped on the way in; a value the sender writes is replaced.

workspace_id.description: A workspace identifier: `ws_` followed by a ULID.

space_id.description: The space, when the event belongs to one.

run_id.description: The run, when the event belongs to one.

seq.description: Assigned by the server on append, monotonic per workspace. Absent on the way in.

idempotency_key.description: Required on every client-originated write. Sending the same key twice is a no-op.

kind.description: Whether a person, a harness, one of a harness's agents or Chips itself acted.

id.description: The participant id, or `system` for Chips.

harness_id.description: For an agent: the harness it speaks through, whose budget and runs are the agent's (ADR 0087). Filled in by Chips.

actor.description: The participant an event is attributed to.

min.description: Oldest major version the server accepts.

max.description: Newest major version the server speaks.

protocol.description: The negotiated range. A client picks a version inside it or is refused.

takes.description: What this server keeps of what a person's client may send beyond the base set, by the names in `SERVER_TAKES`. `held_yes` is `for_minutes` and `until_stopped` on `approval.resolved`. A server older than the field says nothing, and drops those fields, so a client offers neither to it (ADR 0281). `spend_no_cap` is No cap and amounts past $100 on a room's Spend per job (ADR 0292).

server.description: Who the client is talking to.

harness_id.description: A harness identifier: `hrn_` followed by a ULID.

display_name.description: The harness's name in the workspace.

owner_id.description: The person accountable for this harness.

ephemeral.description: True for a transient child minted for one lane, which inherits its lead's settings.

items.description: The harness this connection is, as Chips knows it.

harnesses.description: The harness the token belongs to, and only that one. One connection speaks for all of the harness's agents (ADR 0087), which `agents` lists. A harness running inside another is a lane, not a duplicate.

harness.description: The harness this connection is: `harnesses[0]`, said once. Read this rather than the list.

harness_id.description: A harness identifier: `hrn_` followed by a ULID.

display_name.description: The harness's name in the workspace.

owner_id.description: The person accountable for this harness.

ephemeral.description: True for a transient child minted for one lane, which inherits its lead's settings.

agents.description: The harness's agents, each with its rooms (ADR 0087). Everything the connection sends names one of them as `actor`; a harness's own id is read as its one agent in the room. Sent only to a harness that declares `agents`.

agent_id.description: A agent identifier: `agt_` followed by a ULID.

key.description: The harness's own name for it.

name.description: What it is called, and so its @handle.

lead.description: Whether it is the harness's Main agent.

state.description: Archived when its thing was put away.

items.description: A space identifier: `spc_` followed by a ULID.

spaces.description: The rooms it is in. One at most, once one room per agent is the rule.

room.description: The open room it is in (ADR 0087: one at a time), or `null` while it is free. What it says while free is held.

anyOf.description: A space identifier: `spc_` followed by a ULID.

held.description: How many of its words Chips is holding, said while it was in no room.

items.description: An agent the harness speaks for.

autonomy.description: The level in force for this connection.

policy.description: The rules that fill in the details.

autonomy.description: 0 observe, 1 ask first, 2 ask when it matters, 3 autonomous and report back. Presets that expand to rules.

match.description: A glob over action kinds, for example `payment.*`.

when.description: Extra conditions on the action's flags, and for a command, how its parts start.

items.description: A risk class the policy engine can match a rule against.

starts_with.description: For an action that carries a command (ADR 0239): the words a part of it starts with. A command goes ahead on such rules only when every part starts with one that allows it.

decision.description: What to do when the rule matches.

approvers.description: Who may answer, when the decision is `ask`.

items.description: `owner`, `any`, `lead`, `role:<name>`, or a specific person id; a lead harness's id once resolved.

reason.description: Shown to the harness, and recorded in the audit log.

off.description: Turned off by a person (ADR 0195): kept in the list to turn back on, and skipped by the policy engine until then.

made_by.description: Who made it by answering an ask with Always (ADR 0195). Filled in by Chips.

made_at.description: When a person's answer made it (ADR 0195): Always, or This session. Filled in by Chips. A rule a person's answer made never allows an action that matters.

items.description: A rule the policy engine evaluates.

rules.description: Evaluated in order; the workspace cap always wins.

budget.description: The ceiling, and what has been spent.

spaces.description: The spaces this credential is a member of as it connects. A client that kept a cache drops what is not here: a membership it lost while away is the one event a replay can never bring it, because it is no longer in the space that event belongs to.

items.description: A space identifier: `spc_` followed by a ULID.

workspace.description: The workspace as it is called now. A device keeps the name it was told when it paired and takes this one when they differ, so a workspace renamed since is called by its new name without pairing again. Absent when the workspace has no name.

description: The server's half of the handshake: the protocol range it speaks, and who this connection is.
title: Hello
